## 10aa0e361a4e

**Reproduced lesson-identifiability defect.** Audited source SHA-256:
`375bfcc7bf0305228f04665dc3d79ad8184f6293d89ccdf3b8edf773c95cebd2`.
An independent implementation of “choose the component with maximum 3x3-grown
union area, then crop and paint it 8” reproduces all three canonical outputs.
The cheaper rival “choose the component with the most raw cells, then apply the
same growth/crop” also reproduces all three canonical outputs. The generator
makes raw sizes distinct, so that rival is strongly favored by the curriculum.

Across 3,000 deterministic four-pair lessons (1,000 per band; each pair held out
once as query), the raw-size rival disagreed on 600/12,000 individual pairs and
created **536 teaching failures in 536 lessons**: all three demonstrations fit
the rival while the held-out query required the true grown-area comparison.

The first retained failure is easy band, seed `990001`, sample indexes
`[4,5,6,7]`, query position `2`. Its three demonstrations agree with raw-size
selection. In the query, scan-order raw sizes are `[7,8,6]` but grown areas are
`[26,24,22]`; the true winner is object 0 while the shortcut selects object 1,
producing different cropped outputs. The exact inputs, labels, shortcut outputs,
and component measurements are retained in
`checks/audit/10aa0e361a4e/report.json`; replay code is
`checks/audit/10aa0e361a4e/raw_size_shortcut_probe.py`.

Suggested repair: construct lessons with at least two demonstrations where raw
cell count and grown union area rank different objects, declare the raw-size
rival, and test every allowed query rotation. The measured rival set is finite;
this audit does not claim universal identifiability.
